newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Credit Suisse reports good first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse reports good first quarter.

text.p: Credit Suisse Group, Switzerland's second-biggest banking group, said Monday it was off to a very good start in the first quarter of 1997 and was confident of meeting its mid-term financial goals.
CS Group said revenues from commissions and trading activities were significantly higher than in the year-ago period, while expenses and provisions developed in line with management expectations.
As in the past, CS Group did not provide figures for its first-quarter performance.

A major restructuring at the start of this year created four business areas: domestic retail and corporate bank Credit Suisse, international corporate and investment bank Credit Suisse First Boston, CS Private Banking and CS Asset Managment.

"Credit Suisse Group has started 1997 with a very good first quarter," it said. "All four business units achieved strong earnings improvements compared with the average quarterly operating results for 1996," it added without elaborating.
CS Group said its new corporate structure was proving successful.

"Given the progress to date in the restructuring and the very good start to the year, Credit Suisse Group is confident that it will make significant steps toward achieving its medium-term financial targets in the course of 1997," it said.
Chief Executive Lukas Muehlemann said in March the group's return on equity goal was 15 percent. In 1996 the return on equity, in respect with the operating result, was 10.1 percent.

Credit Suisse's group operating profit after extraordinary items in 1996 eased to 1.638 billion Swiss francs ($1.1 billion) from 1.695 million ($1.15 billion). But due to extraordinary charges for restructuring and for providing for bad loans, the CS Group plunged into a 1996 net loss of 2.59 billion francs ($1.76 billion) compared with a net profit of 1.401 billion ($954 million) in 1995.
CS Private Banking and Asset Management benefited from good financial markets and an increase in the volume of assets under management, the group said.
"Credit Suisse First Boston ... posted significantly higher revenues and results, due mainly to the good conditions in the securities markets in the first two months of the year," it said.
